paras: The Perry Hill church shooting was a fight on a Sunday in September 1903 at the Perry Hill colored church near Bigbyville, Tennessee, in which a white vendor from Columbia, Tom McDonald, struck a Black man and fired into a crowd of Black churchgoers. Lewis Thompson was hit in the hand, and the Columbia Herald headlined the affair "SMALL RACE WAR."

The county's Black Baptists were holding a four-day Association convention at the Perry Hill church. McDonald, who ran the hack line from Columbia to Mt. Pleasant, had turned his hack into a soda pop stand near the church; with him were his father, D. F. Watson and a white boy, Anner Witherspoon.

During the day McDonald quarreled with Dave Jackson, a Black man from Columbia who, according to the Herald, "it is said, refused to pay for a drink." McDonald knocked Jackson down with a blow to the head; the paper said brass knuckles "were much in evidence" but not whether McDonald used them. Churchgoers told McDonald he would have to move, and as he prepared to go, stones struck him or his companions.

By the Herald's account, McDonald warned the crowd, drew a pistol and fired three or four shots, one hitting Thompson on the hand. As the hack pulled away, pursuers pelted it with rocks, and McDonald fired two more shots; a man in the crowd returned fire, and none of these shots took effect. The white party left the hack with its driver, Gibson, and fled through a corn field; the pursuers held the hack until McDonald's party recovered it.
The Herald reported that the Black participants intended to have McDonald's party arrested on Monday, but that by noon nothing had been done, and no later report was found.

The Columbia Herald's front-page story of September 18, 1903, the only coverage found, billed it as a "Shooting Scape With a Crowd of Negroes At a Colored Church." It reported McDonald's blow and the rumor of brass knuckles but presented the gunfire as following his warnings to stone-throwing "angry negroes." No Black-press account was found.

reader.title: Perry Hill church shooting
bases: A1 describes a dispute over payment for a drink in which a white vendor struck a Black customer, was stoned by the church crowd, and fired into it, followed by a chase and an exchange of shots; it was not an organized attack on the community or a mob action.
The Columbia Herald (A1) is the only report found in either press; no second account or follow-up appears.

accounts.label: Local white newspaper
accounts.gist: The Columbia Herald says McDonald struck Jackson over an unpaid drink, was stoned by churchgoers after being told to move, warned them and then fired, and that the party fled under pursuit and a returned shot; several details are hedged with 'it is said' and 'it is stated'.

framing.detail: Headlined 'SMALL RACE WAR' with a deck on McDonald's 'Shooting Scape With a Crowd of Negroes'; it reports McDonald's blow and possible brass knuckles but frames the gunfire as a response to stones after warnings.
